question.text: Which approach best reflects the savings-before-spending principle in personal budgeting?

answer.text: Save whatever is left after meeting all expenses
Prioritize savings by setting aside a fixed amount before spending on discretionary items
Savings and expenses should always be equal
Income should be doubled to ensure adequate savings

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 55 of the workbook says that required savings should be allocated before the figure is spent elsewhere, and that direct transfers should be used so the savings plan becomes a fixed part of the budget. The Trap: Treating savings as the residual left over after all expenses tends to leave the savings figure inadequate; the workbook reverses that order by giving savings first claim on income. Note: A direct transfer mechanism that moves the savings amount out of the spending account at a fixed time helps embed the rule in the regular budget cycle.
